newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi lawyers to appeal to Home Office.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi lawyers to appeal to Home Office.

text.p: Lawyers for former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi said on Wednesday they would turn to Britain's interior ministry after losing an appeal in the London High Court against the transfer of documents to Italy.

The judges, Lord Justice Simon Brown and Mr Justice Gage, on Wednesday rejected all the grounds of the appeal against sending documents to Milan magistrates investigating allegations of fraud and false accounting.
Brown agreed to hear an application by the appellants on Friday morning, which could lead to an appeal to the House of Lords, although legal sources said this was unlikely to succeed.

The hearing stemmed from an appeal by Berlusconi, who is on trial in Milan on corruption charges, his company Fininvest and company president Fedele Confalonieri against a court ruling earlier this year that the papers should be sent to Italy.

Ennio Amodio, Berlusconi's lawyer in Milan, told reporters the Home Office (interior ministry) would play a key role in deciding whether the 15 bags of documents seized from the office of London lawyer David Mills in April would be shipped to Italy.
"The real remedy is the appeal to the Home Office," said Amodio.
"It is now up to the Home Office to carry out an in-depth evaluation of political relations with our country," he added.
Amodio alleged that the Milan's public prosecutor's office had illegally used the contents of the seized documents to justify the arrest of managers at Fininvest.
The appeal lodged with the Home Office would ask it to seek an explanation from the Italian authorities of why the documents had been used by Milan investigators.
"We ask them to ask the Italian authorities for a complete explanation of the reasons which induced them (Milan magistrates) to use documents even before they were sent to Italy," Amodio said.

After the High Court ruling, Brown described the case as a "wide-ranging, multi-faceted, international fraud involving far-reaching allegations against a large number of individuals in connection with an even larger number of companies".

Berlusconi is already being prosecuted on a charge of bribing tax inspectors in return for favourable audits of his companies. He goes on trial on November 21 on separate charges of making illegal payments to disgraced former prime minister Bettino Craxi. He denies all charges.

Berlusconi is accused of acquiescing in payments by Fininvest of 10 billion lire ($6.5 million), alleged to have been channeled to Craxi in 1991 through All Iberian, an offshore company linked to Fininvest.
The documents seized in London relate to the activities of All Iberian and other offshore companies linked to Fininvest.
